Years ago, MacBooks featured a Kensington-style security slot that allowed you to attach a lock cable to tether your laptop to a table leg or similar object. It was most handy in coffee shops, so you didn't have to lug your laptop with you when you went to the counter to grab another drink.

Those slots disappeared long ago, but you can now buy adapters that add a security lock slot to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro…

You have to have been using them for a long time to remember the security slot embedded in the side of your laptop. Those slots were designed for a T-shaped accessory that you inserted and then rotated 90 degrees to lock it into place. The most common designs were a cable that you could run through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived that concept with an adapter that mounts to a corner or edge of your MacBook so you can attach a security lock cable. The adapter uses a two-piece construction with screws to clamp the adapter onto your MacBook.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version alongside the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It's worth emphasizing that these security locks have always been low-security devices, designed to prevent someone from grabbing your MacBook and running off in the few seconds you aren't looking. I used one at smaller coffee shops myself, since I could still see my table when I went up for a tea refill, but I would never rely on it to take my MacBook out of sight.

At $70, the adapter isn't cheap, and you still need to buy a security lock separately. But if you happen to have an old one lying in a drawer, it might just be worth bringing it back into service.
